beginner.title: Electronics Basics & Safety
beginner.description: Start from ZERO knowledge! Learn what electricity is, how circuits work, and basic safety. Perfect for 6th-10th graders who have never done electronics before.
objectives: 1. Understand what electricity is and how it flows
2. Learn voltage, current, and resistance in simple terms
3. Know how to safely work with electronic components
4. Identify basic components: resistor, LED, battery, breadboard
outcomes: 1. Safely assemble your first LED circuit
2. Explain why electricity flows in a closed circuit
prerequisites: School science knowledge (like atoms and energy)
beginner.activity: Build your first working circuit: make an LED light up using a battery and resistor

beginner.title: Meet Arduino - Your First Program
beginner.description: What is Arduino? Meet this amazing microcomputer! Install the software and write your first program - NO coding experience needed!
objectives: 1. Understand what an Arduino is and why it's cool
2. Download and install Arduino IDE (free software)
3. Write and upload your first program
4. Understand the basic structure: setup() and loop()
5. Make your Arduino do something visible (blink an LED)
outcomes: 2. Modify the program to change LED blink speed
3. Explain what setup() and loop() do
prerequisites: Basic computer skills (using mouse, keyboard, files)
topics: 2. Arduino Uno board: tour of all parts
3. IDE: what is it and how to use it
7. Comments: how to explain your code
beginner.activity: Set up your Arduino and make an LED blink on and off

beginner.title: Control Things - Make LEDs Blink Patterns
beginner.description: Learn to control digital outputs! Make LEDs light up in any pattern you want. Traffic light? SOS signal? Create it!
outcomes: 1. Build LED circuit controlled by Arduino
3. Program an SOS morse code flasher
beginner.activity: Build a traffic light controller or SOS flasher with 3 LEDs

beginner.title: Read User Input - Buttons & Switches
beginner.description: Make your projects interactive! Learn to read buttons and switches. Create programs that respond to what YOU do!
objectives: 1. Read digital input from buttons using digitalRead()
3. Make Arduino respond to button presses
outcomes: 2. Create a simple game or quiz with buttons
4. Debug and fix bouncing button issues
topics: 5. Button bounce: what is it and why it matters
beginner.activity: Build a button-controlled traffic light or simple quiz game

beginner.title: Read Sensors - Measure Light, Temperature, Distance
beginner.description: Add sensor superpowers to your Arduino! Measure light, temperature, movement, and distance. Make your projects aware of the world!
objectives: 3. Use light sensor (photoresistor) to detect brightness
5. Create sensor-based decisions in your code
outcomes: 1. Read values from potentiometer or light sensor
2. Control LED brightness based on room light
3. Build a temperature alarm that alerts you
5. Make robots react to their environment
beginner.activity: Build a light-activated LED or temperature alarm system

beginner.title: Control Brightness - PWM Explained Simply
beginner.description: Dim and brighten LEDs smoothly! Control motor speed! Learn PWM - a clever trick that makes things seem brighter or faster without using more power.
objectives: 1. Understand PWM using simple everyday examples
4. Control motor speed with a potentiometer
outcomes: 2. Create breathing or fading light effects
3. Control motor speed with a dial
topics: 1. What is PWM? (Pulse Width Modulation explained simply)
7. Creating smooth fading effects with loops
beginner.activity: Create a breathing LED effect and control motor speed with potentiometer

intermediate.title: Serial Communication - Talk to Your Arduino
intermediate.description: See what your Arduino is thinking! Use Serial Monitor to display values, debug problems, and send commands from your computer to your Arduino.
objectives: 1. Use Serial Monitor to display sensor readings
2. Send text messages from Arduino to computer
3. Receive and understand commands from computer
outcomes: 1. Display live sensor values on your screen
2. Send commands to control your Arduino
topics: 7. Sending text commands (like 'L' for LED ON)
intermediate.activity: Display sensor readings live and control LED via Serial Monitor commands

intermediate.title: Making Things Move - Control Motors
intermediate.description: Build robots that move! Learn how to control DC motors for speed and direction, and servo motors for precise positioning. Build a moving robot car!
objectives: 1. Understand DC motors and how they work
6. Build a simple robot car chassis
outcomes: 1. Make motor spin forward and backward
4. Build and program a robot that moves
topics: 2. H-bridge concept: how to change direction
intermediate.activity: Build a robot car that moves forward, backward, and turns

intermediate.title: Advanced Sensors - Obstacle & Line Sensors
intermediate.description: Add more senses to your robot! Connect distance sensors, motion detectors, and line sensors. Make your robot aware and reactive to its environment!
objectives: 1. Connect ultrasonic distance sensor to detect obstacles
2. Use motion sensors (PIR) to detect movement
3. Add line sensors for autonomous navigation
5. Make decisions based on sensor data
outcomes: 4. Combine multiple sensors in one project
5. Make robots react intelligently to surroundings
prerequisites: Completed analog and digital input modules
topics: 1. Ultrasonic distance sensor (HC-SR04) - how it works
intermediate.activity: Build an obstacle-avoiding robot or line-following robot

intermediate.title: Connecting Modules - I2C Protocol Made Simple
intermediate.description: Connect LCD displays, sensors, and other modules using I2C! Connect many devices with just 2 wires. Add screens to show information!
objectives: 2. Connect I2C LCD display to Arduino
3. Display messages and numbers on LCD
outcomes: 1. Display sensor readings on LCD screen
topics: 3. Pull-up resistors: why we need them
intermediate.activity: Connect LCD display and show live sensor data on screen

advanced.title: Remote Control Your Robot - Bluetooth
advanced.description: Control your robot from your smartphone! Add wireless Bluetooth control. Become a true robot master!
objectives: 1. Connect HC-05 Bluetooth module to Arduino
2. Receive commands from Bluetooth app on phone
3. Send robot status back to phone
outcomes: 1. Remote control robot movement with Bluetooth
2. Receive data on Arduino from phone
5. Create or use existing control app
advanced.activity: Build Bluetooth-controlled robot car that responds to phone commands

resources.title: MIT App Inventor (make Bluetooth app FREE)

advanced.title: Advanced Motor Control - Make Things Move Smart
advanced.description: Control multiple motors with precision! Create robots that follow complex paths and move smoothly. Make smooth, intelligent movements!
objectives: 2. Implement non-blocking timing for complex movements
outcomes: 1. Make robot follow complex paths accurately
2. Run multiple actions at the same time
advanced.activity: Program robot to navigate a maze or follow complex path

advanced.title: Save Your Data - SD Cards & Memory
advanced.description: Never lose data again! Save sensor readings and robot actions to SD cards. Analyze what happened after your project runs!
objectives: 1. Connect SD card module to Arduino
2. Write data to files on SD card
3. Read data back from SD card
outcomes: 1. Save sensor readings to SD card
advanced.activity: Build data logger that records sensor values every minute to SD card

advanced.title: Smart Control - Make Your Robot Learn to Adjust
advanced.description: Make truly intelligent robots! Learn feedback control so your robot automatically adjusts to maintain perfect behavior. Self-correcting robots!
outcomes: 1. Build robot that maintains straight line automatically
prerequisites: Comfortable with basic math and logic
advanced.activity: Build very accurate line-follower or temperature control system

advanced.title: Final Project - Design and Build Your Own Robot!
advanced.description: Bring it ALL together! Design and build YOUR OWN robot project combining everything you learned. From idea to working robot! Present your creation!
objectives: 1. Plan and design your own robot project
2. Combine all learned skills in one project
outcomes: 1. Completed working robot that performs its task
4. Written explanation of how it works
advanced.activity: Design and build ANY robot you want! Ideas: obstacle avoider, line follower, maze solver, bluetooth car, plant waterer, tracker, alarm system, etc.
